main_text.p: Etsi enim nemo fere est, qui non ταῖς[?] προπαθείαις[?] saepius & uehementius quàm expediat & deceat, commoueatur: uult tamen Deus, nos nequaquam indulgere affectibus istis, & non erumpere in facta quae pugnant cum diuina uoluntate. iuxta illud: Irascimini, & ne peccate. Psal.4. 4. Eph.4.26.
Ideo precatur Dauid: Etiam à superbijs (sic uocat effrenes affectus) contine Seruū tuū,ne dominetur mihi. Psal.19.13.

head.i: Sed cur irridere Deus dicitur istos motus cordis humani?

main_text.p: Quia ut maximè in cæteris rebus sapi-ant, qui iftis motibus indulgent: ridiculi tamen sunt, cum & denunciationes diuinas, & earum euetus, suo potius arbitrio, quàm Dei consilio æstimant. Quasi uerò miseri & stolidi homunculi Deo à consilijs esse possimus? Rom.11.34. Si sus Miner-uam doceat, & homo suijpsius oblitus memoriam moneat, sibiq; in eo placeat & adplaudat, an non ridiculus ceseri[?] debet?

head.i: Quinam uerò hoc pacto præ cæte-ris peccant?

main_text.p: Qui nondum plenè didicerunt, in sua statione τῷ ταξιάρχῳ[?] Deo obedire, nec suâ sortem

page.notes: Uncertain readings: the two Greek words in the first paragraph and the Greek word "ταξιάρχῳ" are read from a small, worn scan and need checking against the original. "miseri" is broken across lines ("mi" / "feri") with no printed hyphen visible, so it is written whole. "ceseri" is marked [?] because the long s makes the word hard to read. The question headings are set in italics and centred, so they are given level 3. The small mark at the lower left edge is treated as a stain and left out. The last paragraph continues on the next page.
